summary.headline: Gokul Agro Q2 FY27 revenue up 13% to INR7,481 crore; EBITDA up 41% to INR276 crore with margin at 3.68%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 13% YoY to INR7,481 crore, with EBITDA including other income up 41% to INR276 crore and margin up about 74 bps to 3.68%. PAT rose 40% to INR150 crore, and H1 PAT grew 54% to INR274 crore on 10% revenue growth. Management attributed the growth mainly to better price realisations, with no volume growth expected this year as capacity is fully utilised. A 24 September 2026 change in edible oil import duties deferred trade purchases in September, lifting closing inventory, which management called a timing effect. This was the company's first earnings call, held to start a regular investor engagement.

segments.name: Edible oils
segments.commentary: About 85% of H1 FY27 consolidated volume; palm and soybean are the largest categories, with sunflower, mustard, groundnut, cottonseed, rice bran and vanaspati also sold.

segments.name: Biodiesel
segments.commentary: 300 TPD Gandhidham plant fully operational in Q1 FY27 and ISCC certified; revenue INR237 crore in Q2 and INR596 crore in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Castor derivatives
segments.commentary: Castor oil plus 12-HSA, hydrogenated castor oil and ricinoleic acid; no separate financials disclosed.

segments.name: Specialty fats
segments.commentary: Richfield, Pride, Biscopride, Chocosil and Rich Chef; described as a smaller share of volumes, with no figures given.

segments.name: Channel mix (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: B2B 79%, exports 13% (33 countries), B2C 8% of channel revenue, up from about 5-6% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 10% expected next year, then 10% to 15% per year thereafter, at current commodity prices.
EBITDA margin expected to stay in a 3.5% to 4% range, with absolute EBITDA growing accordingly.
Capacity additions across four plants, about 8 lakh tonnes per annum, operational only by October 2027.
B2C marketing spend earmarked at under INR25 crore, to be spent gradually; B2C margins expected to be broadly in line with consolidated, with no large near-term expansion.
Next earnings calls to follow half-year and full-year results.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity: Gandhidham about 3,400 TPD refining, 3,200 TPD seed crushing and 300 TPD biodiesel; Krishnapatnam about 1,400 TPD refining; Haldia about 1,350 TPD refining; Mangalore facility (capacity not stated).
Capacity expansion of about 8 lakh tonnes per annum across the four manufacturing locations, with full operation expected by October 2027.
15 MW captive solar plant commissioned in Gujarat in Q1 FY27; further 4 MW Andhra Pradesh, 4 MW Karnataka and 10 MW Gujarat planned.
Oil palm: about 550 hectares completed in FY25-26, with 900 hectares under development for completion in FY27; current output about 1,000 tonnes per annum, under 1% of requirement.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the 13% Q2 revenue growth mainly to better price realisations; commodity prices rose 15% to 20%, and realisations track market prices.
Edible oil import duties revised effective 24 September 2026; trade deferred purchases in September, raising closing inventory. Management views this as temporary, with channel activity normalising.
Hedging: inventory largely sold through back-to-back physical forwards or hedged on CBOT and Malaysian exchanges; import payments hedged via forwards; open inventory held at 10% to 15%.

About 80% of raw material is imported. Stock-in-trade purchases rose to INR2,000 crore in Q2 from INR491 crore in Q1; management said trading sales are usually 10% to 20% of volume and under 15% in H1.
Distribution spans more than 650 dealers and distributors across 28 states and UTs, with a new Jammu and Kashmir depot and Vitalife push in Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and Karnataka.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from volume, price and new businesses such as biodiesel?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was driven mainly by better price realisations. Volume growth is not expected this year because capacity is fully utilised; new capex is underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is the roughly 3.5% margin sustainable, or does it include inventory or forex gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, citing branding, value-added mix, better utilisation, smarter sourcing and cost control, with no mention of inventory or forex gains.

qa_highlights.question: How is the business insulated from edible oil price and forex volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is back-to-back sold or hedged, import payments are forward-hedged, and open inventory is held at 10% to 15%. No derivatives are used for forex.

qa_highlights.question: What volume and EBITDA growth is expected over the next three years from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 10% next year and 10% to 15% annually after that, with EBITDA margin at 3.5% to 4%; capacity arrives by October 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are per-tonne realisations and EBITDA by product, and what are B2C margins and spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Product-wise realisations and EBITDA per tonne were not disclosed. B2C margins are roughly in line with consolidated 3.5%, with marketing spend under INR25 crore and FY26 spend not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stock-in-trade purchases rise to INR2,000 crore in Q2, and what is the scale of palm plantation backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports are about 80% of raw material, with surplus vessel quantities sold outright; trading sales are typically under 15%. Palm output is about 1,000 tonnes per annum, under 1% of requirement, with benefits 3 to 4 years away.

risks_watch: Inventory build in Q2 from the import duty change; watch whether the September deferral reverses in Q3 and whether inventory normalises.
Sustainability of margins as edible oil prices fall; management did not quantify the impact of a 20% price decline.
Rising stock-in-trade purchases (INR2,000 crore in Q2 versus INR491 crore in Q1) and their effect on working capital and margins.
No volume growth this year with capacity expansion only by October 2027, so FY28 volume growth depends on execution.
Limited segment disclosure: no product-wise realisations, EBITDA per tonne or castor and specialty fats financials, which limits analysis.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and hedging, with firm forward targets of 10% to 15% volume growth and 3.5% to 4% EBITDA margins. Evasive on product-level realisations, B2C historicals and FY26 marketing spend, which were deferred to a later date. Also brief on the September inventory build, which was framed as temporary.
key_quotes: We are not into speculation, sir.
Considering the present commodity prices across India, we expect volume growth of 10% in the next year and continuously year-on-year also 10% to 15% hence forth.
We therefore view the increase in inventory largely in the context of this temporary timing impact, rather than an indication of structural weakness in underlying demand.

adds.what: About 8 lakh tonnes per annum capacity expansion across four manufacturing locations
15 MW captive solar plant, Gujarat (commissioned Q1 FY27; power, not production capacity)

growth.why: Management guides volume growth of 10% next year and 10-15% thereafter, but says there is no volume growth this year because capacity is fully utilised; the ~8 lakh tpa expansion is only operational by October 2027, so the FY28 volume guide rests on capacity not yet built, and the H1 revenue growth of 10% was mainly price-driven.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin to stay at 3.5% to 4%, versus 3.68% in Q2 and 3.86% in H1, citing branding, value-added mix, utilisation and sourcing; the 74 bps YoY gain was partly price-driven, so the range implies limited further expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 8 lakh tpa across four plants is under construction with full operation by October 2027, and the 15 MW Gujarat solar plant was already commissioned in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 10% volume growth next year and 10-15% after, but says no volume growth this year because capacity is fully utilised, so FY28 depends on the October 2027 capacity arriving.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is at full optimum capacity and about 8 lakh tpa is already under way, but no further capex was guided beyond it, so a new round is plausible though not explicitly planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was set as new ranges (10-15% volume, 3.5-4% margin) with no volume growth this year, and H1 revenue growth of 10% was mainly price-driven, so there is little room to raise volume guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margins are at the top of the range and the September import duty change pushed inventory up, with management not quantifying the impact of a 20% edible oil price fall; stock-in-trade rose to INR2,000 crore in Q2 from INR491 crore in Q1.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: B2C is growing (5-6% of channel revenue in FY26 to 8% in H1 FY27) with under INR25 crore marketing earmarked and a Vitalife push, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Reversal of September inventory build
rows.why: Import duty change on 24 September 2026 deferred trade purchases and lifted closing inventory; management calls it temporary, but whether it reverses in Q3 is unconfirmed.

rows.label: Export and B2C expansion
rows.why: Exports are 13% of H1 channel revenue across 33 countries and B2C rose to 8% from 5-6% in FY26, but no targets were given beyond the INR25 crore B2C spend.

rows.label: Palm plantation backward integration
rows.why: Palm output is about 1,000 tpa, under 1% of requirement, with 900 hectares under development and benefits 3 to 4 years away, so it will not move near-term fundamentals.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, hedging and the 10-15% volume and 3.5-4% margin targets, but evasive on product-level realisations, B2C historicals and FY26 marketing spend, which were deferred.
